title: SPLA/97/2012 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND Vs PREM RAM AND ORS

paras.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Special Leave to Appeal No. 97 of 2012
In
Government Appeal No. 34 of 2012
With
Delay Condonation Application No. 1248 of 2012

State of Uttarakhand. .......... Appellant
Versus
Prem Ram & others. .......... Respondents
Mr. A.S. Gill, Government Advocate, with Ms. Shiwali Joshi, Brief Holder, for the
State of Uttarakhand / appellant.
Mr. R.C. Tamta, Advocate for the respondents.

Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
 There has been 17 days' delay in preferring the appeal. The
learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents has no objection,
if the Application for condonation of delay is allowed. We have
independently considered the averments made in the Application for
condonation of delay and, being satisfied with the reasons furnished
therein, allow the same.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties on the Application for
grant of special leave to prefer appeal.
3. This was a case covered under Section 302 as well as under
Section 304-B and 498-A of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3/4 of
the Dowry Prohibition Act. According to the learned Government
Advocate, the post mortem report, not under challenge before the court
below, clearly revealed that it was a case of homicide. According to the

2
learned Government Advocate, this aspect of the matter has not been
addressed at all while rendering the judgment and order under appeal. We
are satisfied that the matter requires re-consideration by the appellate
court and, accordingly, allow the Application for grant of special leave to
prefer appeal.
4. The appeal is admitted. Let the lower court records be called
for. Registry is directed to prepare paper-books no sooner the lower court
records are received. Permission is granted to request for fixation of an
early date of hearing as soon as the paper-books are made ready and
exchanged.

(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
 24.12.2012 24.12.2012
G
